A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Augur. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments, automatic and human narrative evaluations, ablations, sensitivity studies, and appendix feature-selection results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds physics-based and synthetic causal-discovery results, plus an LLM-as-a-Judge narrative evaluation.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, graph pruning/judgment/refinement, explanation filtering, and the fine-tuning objective remain unchanged. The auxiliary-parser disclosure and new inference paragraph clarify existing operations; autonomous downstream student inference was already described in v1’s Appendix E.

E1.justification: Section 5.6 adds direct causal-graph recovery evaluation using physics-based annotations of Power scenarios and a new eight-variable noisy VAR dataset containing lagged terms and confounders. This substantially extends evaluation beyond the retained forecasting and narrative tasks across four real-world domains.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Time-VLM. New Tables 5–6 introduce PC, GES, MI, Granger causality, and PCMCI as evaluated causal-discovery comparators, adding a substantial new comparison family. GPT4TS becomes GPT4MTS with the same citation and scores, indicating a naming correction rather than another added baseline.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate annotated and synthetic graphs using precision, recall, F1, and structural Hamming distance, and score narratives with an LLM judge. Section 5.1 also replaces v1’s time-step/static text description with exclusively static dataset descriptions and variable definitions, barring external/future information. This establishes a reported setting revision without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a teacher-versus-student cost and latency analysis, while Appendix D.1.2 adds a supplementary automated assessment of narrative quality. Existing component ablations, narrative-granularity and data-scaling studies, correlation-threshold analysis, feature-selection study, and wind-power case study are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that reported metrics average five independent runs. v2 introduces no new seed disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: New Tables 5–6 report Augur F1/SHD of 0.34/9.3 on physics-based graphs and 0.64/9.4 on synthetic graphs; PCMCI achieves lower synthetic SHD, 5.2. Table 8 adds judge averages of 6.15 on Power and 6.14 on Air. Time-VLM scores and teacher/student efficiency estimates are also added. Matched pre-existing forecasting, narrative, human-evaluation, ablation, and feature-selection values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–18, Appendix A’s causal definitions, and Appendix B’s causal-feature-optimality theorem and proof are retained. The added empirical graph metrics introduce no new formal result or derivation.

C1.justification: The central novelty, forecasting, interpretability, and zero-shot generalization claims remain. v2 emphasizes efficiency and scalability in the introduction and conclusion, but these benefits were already claimed in v1’s method discussion and Appendix E.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies physics-based ground truth as state-dependent and interprets high graph precision as protecting student training from false causal prompts. It also discusses substituting efficient models for atomic judgments and adds prospective societal applications. The original limitations concerning confounding, correlation-based pruning, and teacher knowledge remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents student-only inference, auxiliary parsing for groundedness, task-specific retraining, and teacher/student inference costs and latency. It supplies the LLM-judge prompt and replaces Appendix C.2’s conflicting Gemma-2B identification with a generic lightweight model description. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, and the promised future corpus release remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Time-VLM, TFB, temporal causal discovery, mutual information, PCMCI, and Granger causality. These support the expanded comparisons, while the related-work narrative and principal novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized wording and punctuation edits, a rewritten implementation paragraph and conclusion, and added inference, RQ5, judge-evaluation, and societal-impact passages. The overall section structure and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5, 6, and 8 and a Time-VLM row in Table 1. Human and automatic narrative-evaluation tables exchange order and numbering, and other displays relocate as text expands. Figures 1–9 retain their content and design; the overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: Section 5.6 provides direct quantitative checks of causal recovery that v1 lacked, and the added judge evaluation and inference details improve validation and clarity. The benefit is limited by missing sample counts and generator/settings details for the new causal benchmarks, and limited measurement context for the efficiency estimates. These additions modestly strengthen the paper without fully resolving the evidential and reproducibility gaps around its causal claims.
